1efk7g5: Many restaurants in Latin America and Spain have a **menú del día**: a fixed price with a **first course** (de primero), a **second course** (de segundo), **dessert**, and sometimes a **drink**. If you want to see all the dishes, you ask for **la carta** (in Latin America it is also called **el menú**).
1fjk1va: With the waiter you normally use **usted**. The most useful phrases are: **Para mí, la sopa**; **De primero, la ensalada, y de segundo, el pollo**; **¿Me trae un agua, por favor?**; **¿Me puede traer otra servilleta?**; **¿Qué me recomienda?**
13fe4f9: To ask about a dish: **¿El arroz lleva carne?** (_llevar_ = to have as an ingredient), **¿Es picante?** For a change: **Sin cebolla, por favor.** At the end: **La cuenta, por favor** or **¿Nos trae la cuenta?** And if you want to know how to pay: **¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?**
1kb8y0q: The waiter also uses set phrases: **¿Qué quieren tomar?** (to drink), **¿Algo más?**, **Ahora le traigo la cuenta.** In _le traigo_, **le** means _a usted_: learn it as a block.
zuqcsc: **Variation.** The person who serves is called **mesero/mesera** in Mexico and Central America, **camarero/camarera** in Spain, **mozo/moza** in Argentina and Uruguay, and **mesonero/mesonera** in Venezuela. In Central America, a **fresco** is a natural fruit or cocoa drink (in Mexico, _agua fresca_; in other countries, _jugo_ or _zumo_).
ef7vic: You say **un agua** and **el agua**, even though _agua_ is feminine (_el agua fría_). This happens with feminine words that begin with a stressed **a**.
1vz0nfm: It's a translation of _Can I have…?_. In Spanish you ask them to **bring** you something: _¿Me trae…?_ or simply _La cuenta, por favor_.
1vd2rm0: After _para_, **mí** (pronoun) takes an accent mark. _Mi_ without an accent is possessive: _mi plato_.
1vm4bk7: With _sin_ you don't need _nada_: **sin carne**. _Nada de_ goes with _no_: _No tiene nada de carne_.

9xynad: You already know **mucho** and **muy**. Now you complete the scale of quantity: **nada de** → **poco** → **un poco de** → **bastante** → **mucho** → **demasiado**.
4rgyvo: **Before a noun**, _poco_, _mucho_, and _demasiado_ agree with it: **poca sal**, **pocos turistas**, **demasiada gente**, **demasiados platos**. _Bastante_ only changes in the plural: **bastante arroz**, **bastantes mesas**. _Un poco de_ doesn't change: **un poco de pan**, **un poco de agua**.
16dmsiy: **Before an adjective or after a verb**, they never change: **La sopa es bastante picante**, **El café es demasiado dulce**, **Como poco**. For adjectives use **un poco** without _de_: **un poco caro**.
n21cnc: **Poco** and **un poco** don't mean the same thing. _Hay poca sopa_ is negative: it's not enough. _Hay un poco de sopa_ is positive: there is some. And **demasiado** always means "more than needed": _demasiado picante_ is a problem, _muy picante_ is just a description.
12wt5tg: **Nada de** works like _nunca_: if it comes after the verb, you need **no** before it: **No tiene nada de carne.**

r5d234: Spanish vowels are **strong** (a, e, o) or **weak** (i, u). When an unstressed weak vowel goes next to another vowel, the two form **a single syllable**: it's a **diphthong**. _Bue-no_, _ciu-dad_, _cuen-ta_, _a-gua_, _sie-te_.
184dkjc: Two strong vowels together go in **separate syllables**: it's a **hiatus**. _Le-ón_, _te-a-tro_, _pa-se-o_. There is also a hiatus when the weak vowel carries the stress: then it takes an **accent mark**: _dí-a_, _pa-ís_, _frí-o_, _Ma-rí-a_.
vdz9wv: You already know many diphthongs: verbs with vowel change create them. _Quiero_, _pienso_, _puedo_, _cuesta_, _recomienda_: the **ie** and the **ue** are pronounced together, in a single beat of voice.
1mruyoc: In the fast, familiar speech of many countries (Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean, Andalusia), some hiatuses become diphthongs: _teatro_ sounds almost like "tia-tro" and _pelear_ almost like "pe-liar". It's normal on the street, but to start, pronounce the full hiatus.
1dqvji6: The accent mark on **í** or **ú** always indicates a hiatus: _día_, _país_, _Raúl_. Without an accent mark, _i_ and _u_ next to another vowel form a diphthong: _piano_, _ciudad_.
